excerpt: A site trailer scope has to account for mud, plan-room paper, and shared restrooms that a standard office checklist ignores. Here is a task-by-task daily, weekly, and monthly scope with realistic labor hours and the specialty items that push a trailer above normal office rates.
quickAnswer: A construction trailer field office scope should cover nightly entry scraping, hard-floor damp mopping, restroom sanitation, trash and recycling, and breakroom wipe-downs, plus weekly dusting of plan tables and HVAC grilles and monthly or quarterly floor buffing. Expect production of 1,800-2,400 sq ft per hour instead of the 3,500 sq ft ISSA office benchmark, so a 1,440 sq ft double-wide takes about 0.6-0.8 labor hours per visit plus restroom time.

blocks.text: What Makes a Trailer Scope Different From a Standard Office Checklist

Most janitorial scopes are written for carpeted suites where soil arrives on office shoes. A construction field office gets soil from steel-toe boots that just crossed a laydown yard, plus silica and drywall dust that drifts through door gaps and settles on every horizontal surface. Plan tables, plotters, and file racks hold paper dust. The breakroom feeds a rotating crew. Restrooms see far more users than the trailer's desk count. A useful scope therefore lists entry soil control and dust management as their own task lines rather than burying them inside 'vacuum and mop'.

Writing the scope line by line also protects you when the vendor bills. If 'scrape and mop entry landing interior' is a nightly task, you can hold the crew to it during a muddy week. If it is not written down, a vendor can call it extra work and charge specialty hourly rates of $55-$95 instead of standard rates of $35-$65.

items: Scrape and sweep the entry vestibule and first 10-15 ft of flooring before any wet work, then damp mop with a neutral cleaner.
Dust-mop and damp-mop VCT or sheet vinyl in the main open area, walking paths, and around the plan table.
HEPA-vacuum carpet tiles in private offices and conference corners, with spot treatment for mud stains.
Empty deskside and central trash, replace liners, and move recycling to the designated roll-off or tote area per the site logistics plan.
Clean and sanitize restroom toilets, urinals, sinks, and counters; restock tissue, towels, and soap; mop restroom floors with disinfectant.
Wipe breakroom counters, sink, microwave inside and out, coffee station, and refrigerator handles.
Disinfect high-touch points: door levers, light switches, sign-in kiosk or tablet stand, shared phones, and printer panels.

blocks.title: Labor hour math
blocks.text: At the ISSA benchmark of 3,500 sq ft per hour, a 1,440 sq ft trailer would take about 25 minutes. Real trailer production of 1,800-2,400 sq ft per hour puts the floor and general cleaning at 36-48 minutes, and two restrooms add 12-20 more, for roughly 0.8-1.1 labor hours per visit. At $35-$65 per hour that is $28-$72 in direct labor, which is why the $90-$135 per-visit minimum still governs pricing on smaller trailers.
Specialty Tasks That Push Labor Above Standard Office Rates

Certain trailer tasks justify specialty pricing because they require different equipment, more time, or extra caution. Separate them in the scope so they are priced deliberately and not absorbed into an underfunded base rate that leads to skipped work.

items.name: Heavy mud recovery
items.text: After rain events or earthwork phases, floors may need a wet-vac pass and a second mop rinse. Price this as a per-event add-on at specialty hourly rates rather than raising the base for the whole year.

items.name: Silica-aware dust control
items.text: Dry sweeping fine construction dust puts it back in the air. Require HEPA vacuums and damp microfiber methods, and ask the vendor to confirm its crew uses them in the trailer.

items.name: Pre-walkthrough detailing
items.text: Owner, lender, or inspector visits often call for a one-time detail of windows, blinds, and walls. Pre-negotiate an hourly rate for these short-notice requests.

items.name: Demobilization clean
items.text: Leasing companies may charge cleaning fees on returned units. A final clean with floor scrub and restroom descaling typically takes 3-6 labor hours for a double-wide.

items.name: Hazardous waste segregation
items.text: Crews should never bag solvent rags, aerosol cans, or batteries with regular trash. Write in that these stay in the GC's designated containers and are excluded from janitorial disposal.

blocks.text: Tools That Make the Trailer Scope Faster

Trailer floors are small and cluttered, so a compact flat mop beats a full bucket-and-wringer setup. The Bona Commercial System multi-surface mop kit uses an 18-inch base on a telescoping aluminum handle with two washable microfiber pads, one for dust and one for damp work, and its wood-safe formula approach also works on vinyl and laminate. For airborne dust, a Medify MA-50 with True HEPA H13 filtration covers up to about 1,100 sq ft per its rating, runs as low as 36 dBA, and offers four fan speeds, which suits the main room of a double-wide. A Winix 5500-2 with True HEPA plus washable AOC carbon handles a 360 sq ft private office or breakroom and helps with diesel and coffee odors. Purifiers are owner-supplied equipment; the scope should specify that the crew wipes housings weekly and logs filter condition for the superintendent.

blocks.title: Keep the scope phase-adjustable
blocks.text: Write a clause allowing frequency and specialty tasks to step down when the project moves from sitework into interior finishes. Soil load can drop by half once paving is complete, and your scope should reflect it.

List what the janitorial vendor will not do: servicing portable toilets and hand-wash stations (sanitation rental vendor), cleaning exterior stairs, ramps, and landings beyond a sweep, washing trailer exterior siding or windows, and removing construction debris, pallets, or packaging from the jobsite. Also exclude moving or touching survey equipment, drawing sets marked for record, and IT closets. Clear exclusions prevent disputes when a foreman asks the night crew to haul a box of cut-offs to the dumpster.

faqs.q: How many labor hours does a construction trailer cleaning take?
faqs.a: Plan on roughly 0.8-1.1 labor hours per visit for a 1,440 sq ft double-wide with two restrooms. That reflects production of 1,800-2,400 sq ft per hour because of mud and dust, versus the 3,500 sq ft per hour ISSA benchmark for typical offices. A 400 sq ft single-wide with one restroom often takes 25-35 minutes.

faqs.q: Should the janitorial vendor clean portable toilets on the jobsite?
faqs.a: Usually no. Portable toilets and hand-wash stations are serviced by the sanitation rental company, which pumps waste and restocks under its own contract. Keep them out of the janitorial scope unless the vendor is licensed and equipped for that work, and state the exclusion in writing.

faqs.q: What chemicals should be used in a construction trailer?
faqs.a: A neutral-pH floor cleaner for VCT, an EPA-registered disinfectant for restrooms and high-touch points, and a glass and surface cleaner cover most needs. Ask for safety data sheets for every product brought on site so the GC can include them in the site HazCom program, and favor Green Seal certified general cleaners where possible.

faqs.q: How often should trailer floors be buffed or extracted?
faqs.a: Quarterly is typical for trailers with heavy boot traffic. VCT buffing or a light recoat takes 60-90 minutes on a double-wide, and carpet tile extraction takes 45-60 minutes. Amortized, that is about $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month.

faqs.q: Can I reduce the scope during slow phases of the project?
faqs.a: Yes, if the contract allows it. Include a frequency step-down clause tied to project milestones, such as dropping from 3x/week to 2x/week once the site is paved. Monthly costs follow the visits-per-month math: 13 visits at 3x/week versus 8.66 visits at 2x/week.
